language_specific.verb: Помочь is perfective; its imperfective partner is помогать. Помогите has stress on и and requests help with a completed task; it can take a dative person and an infinitive, here открыть.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: г is soft before stressed и.
language_specific.usage: Открыть дверь names the task for which help is requested.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular masculine inanimate, identical in form to the nominative; the requested item.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: ч is soft; the following е is stressed.
language_specific.usage: Можно followed by the item is a short request; пожалуйста makes it polite.

language_specific.morphology: Plural form used as a noun; names what the addressee may have.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: ч is soft in the чн cluster; stress falls on и.
language_specific.usage: Наличные means money in cash, as opposed to payment by card.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular masculine inanimate; direct object of оплачу.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: сч is pronounced as a long soft щ sound; ё marks stress.
language_specific.usage: Оплатить счёт means to pay the bill.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative plural of masculine овощ.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: щ is long and soft; the first о is stressed and the second о is reduced.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine; agrees with чистый.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: р is soft before stressed е, while final ц is hard.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular masculine inanimate; direct object of положи.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: п is soft before stressed е; ц is hard.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular feminine; names the available food.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: ш is hard; the first а is stressed.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular feminine in a food request.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: in яичницу, written чн is pronounced шн; stress falls on и.
language_specific.usage: Можно introduces a request; без хлеба specifies that no bread is wanted.

language_specific.morphology: Instrumental singular neuter; names what is spread on the bread.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: с and л are both pronounced in the сл cluster; the first а is stressed.
language_specific.usage: Мазать хлеб маслом means to spread butter on bread.

language_specific.morphology: Prepositional singular masculine after в, indicating location.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: ш remains hard before е; у is stressed.
language_specific.usage: В душе refers to the shower as the source of the water.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular neuter; agrees with сухое.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: т is soft before stressed е; ц is hard before е.
Target: с is soft before ю; the final а is stressed.
language_specific.usage: Сюда gives the destination of положи.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular neuter; agrees with полотенце.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: ч is soft before stressed и; с and т are pronounced in the ст cluster.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine; names what may be present.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: л is soft before и; ф and т are both pronounced in the final cluster.

language_specific.morphology: Accusative singular masculine inanimate; direct object of выключи.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: в is soft before е in the initial св cluster.
language_specific.usage: Выключи свет means to turn off the light.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine; agrees with чемодан.
language_specific.pronunciation: Target: т is soft before я, but ж is hard before ё; ё marks stress.

language_specific.morphology: Доброе is nominative singular neuter, agreeing with утро.
language_specific.usage: A morning greeting suitable for addressing Анна Ивановна respectfully.

language_specific.usage: A polite daytime greeting suitable for addressing Мария Сергеевна.

language_specific.morphology: Добрый is nominative singular masculine, agreeing with вечер.

A farewell anticipating another meeting tomorrow.

language_specific.morphology: Спокойной ночи has genitive singular feminine forms in this fixed wish.
language_specific.usage: A bedtime wish addressed here to children.

language_specific.morphology: Большое is the neuter singular form used in this fixed expression.
language_specific.usage: An emphatic expression of thanks; за introduces what the speaker is grateful for.

common.sentence: Спасибо за чай! — Не за что.

language_specific.morphology: Plural or polite singular imperative, used to address the person whose seat was taken.
language_specific.verb: Простить is perfective; the imperfective partner is прощать. Прости́те has stress on и; it can take an accusative person. The imperative asks for forgiveness for a completed act.

language_specific.morphology: Мне is dative singular; жаль is an impersonal predicative.
language_specific.usage: Expresses sympathy about the situation introduced by что.

language_specific.morphology: Plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Повторить is perfective; the imperfective partner is повторять. Повтори́те has stress on и; it takes an accusative object, here адрес. The imperative requests one repetition.

language_specific.usage: Modifies скажите: the speaker asks to hear the same thing again.

language_specific.morphology: Comparative form of the adverb медленно.
language_specific.usage: Modifies говорите and asks the listener to reduce their speaking speed.

language_specific.morphology: Negated past singular masculine; a female speaker would use не поняла.
language_specific.verb: Понять is perfective; the imperfective partner is понимать. По́нял has stress on the first syllable; понять takes an accusative object, here вопрос. The past form reports a failure to understand.

language_specific.morphology: Third-person singular present; слово is the subject.
language_specific.verb: Значить is imperfective in the sense ‘mean’, with no simple aspectual partner. Зна́чит has stress on the first syllable; что asks for the meaning. The present form asks what the word means.

language_specific.usage: With как, asks for the Russian equivalent of the word under discussion.

language_specific.morphology: Third-person singular present reflexive form; имя is the subject.
language_specific.verb: Писаться is imperfective here, with no simple partner for asking about a spelling. Пи́шется has stress on и; как asks for the manner of writing. The present form asks how the name is normally spelled.

language_specific.usage: Мне плохо states that the speaker feels unwell; мне identifies the person experiencing the condition.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine inanimate; the place being located.

language_specific.usage: With стоит, asks for the price of the ticket.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: The question word Сколько can carry the main stress; the contour commonly falls after it.

language_specific.usage: Asks for the time at which the Russian lesson begins.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Когда can carry the main stress in this information question; the contour commonly falls after it.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative interrogative pronoun asking for a person's identity.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Кто can carry the main stress in this question; the contour commonly falls after it.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine, agreeing with зонт.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: In the yes-or-no question, a rise on ваш can focus the question on whose umbrella it is; the reply confirms ownership.

language_specific.morphology: Indeclinable masculine noun, used here to identify the drink.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: Чай can carry a rising contour in the yes-or-no question; ко́фе carries the corrective focus in the reply, with a falling contour.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular feminine inanimate; identifies what is there.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: In the reply, апте́ка is the new information and can receive the main phrase stress with a falling contour.

language_specific.morphology: На governs prepositional singular столе for a location.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: The reply answers where the key is, so столе́ can carry the main phrase stress with a falling contour.
Sentence: За́втра answers the question about time and can carry the main stress in the reply, with a falling contour.
Sentence: The question can rise on за́втра; сего́дня is the correction in the reply and can carry a falling contour.

language_specific.usage: Adds urgency to the confirmed need for a doctor.

language_specific.morphology: Plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Вызвать is perfective; the imperfective partner is вызывать. Вы́зовите has stress on the first syllable; it takes an accusative object, here скорую. The imperative requests that an ambulance be called.

language_specific.usage: A warning to take care because the water is hot.

language_specific.morphology: Plural or polite singular imperative.
language_specific.verb: Подождать is perfective; ждать is the related imperfective verb. Подожди́те has stress on и. Минуту gives the duration in the accusative; the imperative requests a short wait.

language_specific.morphology: Impersonal можно with the infinitive войти asks permission.
language_specific.verb: Войти is perfective; the imperfective partner is входить. Войти́ has final stress. It describes one directed entry on foot; в- indicates movement inward. It has no object here, and можно asks permission for the prospective action.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A rise on войти́ can mark this as a yes-or-no permission question.

language_specific.usage: Asks whether the place indicated by здесь is available to sit in.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A rise on свобо́дно can mark the question; the reply invites the speaker to sit.

language_specific.morphology: Без governs genitive singular газа.
language_specific.usage: Describes the requested water as non-carbonated.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular feminine inanimate; нужна agrees with помощь.
language_specific.usage: С дверью specifies what the speaker needs help with.

language_specific.morphology: Third-person singular present; голова is the subject.
language_specific.verb: Болеть is imperfective in the sense ‘hurt’, with no simple perfective partner for the ongoing state. Боли́т has final stress; у меня identifies the person experiencing the pain. The present form describes current pain.

language_specific.morphology: Past singular masculine; a female speaker would use потеряла.
language_specific.verb: Потерять is perfective; the imperfective partner is терять. Потеря́л has stress on я; it takes an accusative object, here телефон. The past form reports a completed loss.

language_specific.morphology: Nominative singular masculine, agreeing with автобус.
language_specific.pronunciation: Sentence: A rise on мой can focus the yes-or-no question on whether this is the speaker's bus; ваш confirms it in the reply.
